stem_bark.text: The bark of Benkara malabarica is brown greyish-coloured and lenticellate.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Benkara malabarica is brown greyish-coloured and lenticellate.

seed.text: The seed of Benkara malabarica is subglobose with a flat side. The seed is 6-7 mm across. There are 2 seeds per fruit.
seed.text_html: The seed of Benkara malabarica is subglobose with a flat side. The seed is 6-7 mm across. There are 2 seeds per fruit.

fruit.text: The fruit of Benkara malabarica is a globose berry . The fruit is about 0.8-1 cm across with a 1-1.5 cm long peduncle. It is glossy and bright red when ripe with a crown of persistent calyx lobes. The fruit contains usually 2 seeds.

flower.text: The flowers of Benkara malabarica are axillary corymbose cymes. The calyx-tube is turbinate, 5 mm long and 2-3 mm wide with 5 triangular teeth. The corolla is white and composed of a 4-5 mm long tube and 5 recurved lobes. The androecium is composed of 5 stamens. The filaments are 0.5 mm long and the anthers are filiform and 6-7 mm long. The pistil is composed of a 5 mm long style and a fusiform and 6 mm long stigma . The flowers are fragrant.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Benkara malabarica are axillary corymbose cymes.
The calyx-tube is turbinate, 5 mm long and 2-3 mm wide with 5 triangular teeth.
The corolla is white and composed of a 4-5 mm long tube and 5 recurved lobes.
The androecium is composed of 5 stamens. The filaments are 0.5 mm long and the anthers are filiform and 6-7 mm long.
The pistil is composed of a 5 mm long style and a fusiform and 6 mm long stigma. The flowers are fragrant.

leaf.text: The leaves of Benkara malabarica grow opposite on the stem (decussate). The leaf is simple, bright green-coloured above and paler beneath. The leaf is coriaceous, shiny and glabrous on both sides. The leaves have a 5-6 mm long petiole . The leaf of Benkara malabarica is 4-7 cm long and 2-4 cm wide. The shape of the blade is very variable, from rounded to oblanceolate, the apex is obtuse with a tiny mucro, the base is cuneate and the margins are entire. The venation of the leaf is pinnate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Benkara malabarica is a thorny and deciduous shrub growing up to 6-7 m high. It has axillary and straight paired spines.
habit.text_html: Benkara malabarica is a thorny and deciduous shrub growing up to 6-7 m high. It has axillary and straight paired spines.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Benkara malabarica is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Benkara malabarica is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Benkara malabarica are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Benkara malabarica is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Benkara malabarica is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Benkara malabarica are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

phenology.text: From February to July. From May to December. From September to December. During the hot season. ( This phenology applies to southeastern Indian plains )

reforestation.text: Benkara malabarica is a light demander and drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Benkara malabarica is a light demander and drought resistant. It will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
